name: Latvia: participant-facing document QC
when: After medical, legal, privacy and Latvian-language review, before upload to CTIS.
item_format: Each result records the item id, the outcome, a short rationale and evidence (quoted passage and source locator) or an explicit gap.

items.check: Trial title, sponsor protocol number, EU CT number, sponsor, study centre, treatment names, groups, dose schedule, randomisation ratio, placebo use, blinding and participation period match the current protocol.
Visit schedule, procedures, sample volumes, imaging, questionnaires, optional procedures, follow-up and burden reconcile with the schedule of activities.
Risks match the current protocol, Investigator's Brochure, product information and risk assessment; no applicable reproductive, genetic, radiation, procedural, privacy or withdrawal risk is omitted.
Expected benefit is stated accurately; no personal benefit is implied where none is expected.
Alternatives to participation and usual-care options match the protocol and the Latvian site pathway.
Trial medicines, administration devices and protocol-required medicines, devices and examinations are described as free to the participant where applicable under Latvian rules.
No trial-specific procedure occurs before valid consent, except within an authorised emergency pathway.
Required participation statements are separate from optional choices.
Every optional box can be answered independently and refusal does not create an unintended exclusion.
Signatures and dates match the actual consent pathway: participant or authorised decision-maker, person conducting the interview, and an impartial witness only when applicable.
States that adequate time is given, questions can be asked and a copy of the signed consent record is provided.
Withdrawal from participation is explained separately from withdrawal of optional future-use permission.
Explains what happens to data and samples already collected when consent is withdrawn, without promising deletion where lawfully retained trial records must remain.

sections.title: Population and document coverage
sections.instruction: Map every inclusion pathway in the protocol to a Latvian information and consent document (requirements.json population_sets).

items.check: Every protocol population maps to a Latvian information and consent document (population x document table; populations mutually exclusive within each consent stage).
Healthy volunteers: screening, washout, confinement, restrictions, payments, incidental findings and medical-care wording checked against the Latvia healthy volunteer guide.
Ages 0 to 13: legal-representative consent and age-appropriate child information where the child can understand it.
Ages 14 to 17: both the legal representative's written consent and the minor's own written consent.
Adults unable to consent: lawful decision-maker and participant-information pathway verified against the Latvia legal representative guide.
Emergency enrolment: every Article 35 condition and the subsequent-consent process verified against the Latvia emergency enrollment guide.
Participants unable to write: alternative method and witness signatures verified against the Latvia impartial witness guide.
Pregnancy follow-up: participant and partner pathways kept separate, checked against the Latvia pregnancy follow-up guide.
Controller and relevant processors identified without confusing sponsor, site and investigator roles.
Data categories, purposes, recipients, retention, international transfers, safeguards and applicable rights described consistently with the data-protection statement (LV-R1).
Data State Inspectorate contact details included, as requested by the Latvia national overview.
Direct access to medical records explained for authorised sponsor representatives, investigators, monitors, auditors, inspectors and authorities, only to the extent applicable.
Privacy wording does not present consent to participate as the sole legal basis for every research-processing activity.
Contact details for privacy questions are separate from medical-emergency contacts.
Each sample type, volume, timing, storage location, responsible entity, transfer, retention period, analysis and disposal plan matches the protocol and laboratory manual.
Protocol-required sample use is separate from optional future or secondary research.
Coding or pseudonymisation explained accurately; coded samples are not called anonymous.
States whether genetic analysis is included and whether individual or incidental findings may be returned.
Withdrawal wording aligned across the consent form, biological-samples statement (LV-S1), protocol and sample-management plan.
Optional future use reviewed against the Latvia secondary-use consent guide.
Participant-facing documents are in Latvian and understandable to the intended age and population.
Participant- and doctor-facing recruitment materials are in Latvian.
Study-centre name and address, data-controller identity, ZVA contact, assigned ethics-committee contact and Data State Inspectorate contact included.
Document title, version, date, sponsor protocol number and EU CT number included.
Reimbursement and payment wording reconciles with the participant-compensation template (LV-P1) and the draft site budget (LV-P2).
Injury and insurance wording reconciles with the submitted Latvia-compliant insurance evidence (LV-O1).
The blank CTIS forms contain no participant signatures, completed personal data, tracked changes, comments or drafting notes.
Where a participant group cannot understand Latvian, an additional approved language version and consent process are planned; no ad hoc translation.
Short sentences, familiar Latvian terms, clear headings and sufficient space around consent choices and signatures.
Risk wording is understandable without reducing medical accuracy.
Abbreviations defined at first use; technical detail that does not help the decision removed.
Names, telephone numbers, email addresses, after-hours contacts and site fields reviewed.
Page numbers, headers, footers, version control and filenames consistent.
Final native-language proofread done after all content changes; not only back-translation or automated checks.

sections.title: Signature, version and administration
sections.source: Latvia Part II checklist item 3 and the TrialAgents final-form rules (conventions/template-instructions.md)

items.check: Correct document title, population, language code, version and date.
Version references inside the consent form match the information sheet.
No participant, representative, witness or interviewer signature in the blank CTIS submission copy.
Complete signature and date fields for use at consent for every signer of the pathway.
Witness and interpreter fields only where the witness pathway can apply.
Representative identity, authority or relationship field where a representative signs.
From age 14 the minor's own signature and date block is separate from the legal representative's; a younger child's assent block does not look like legal consent.
Statement that the participant or representative receives a copy of the signed consent documentation.
Correct CTIS section and naming convention; the filename identifies the document type (adult, legal representative, 0 to 13 years, 14 to 17 years).
No personal data that should not appear in the CTIS upload.
No drafting instruction remains in the final version (italic notes, [bracket] notes, ........... gaps, yellow [INSERT/IF/OTHERWISE/CHOOSE/NOTE] labels).
